clue.text: Perhaps keep drier one side rather than the other

indicators.text: one side rather than the other
indicators.note: left and right are the two sides, so the letter for left gives way to the letter for right

parts.note: a towel is something you dry yourself with

explanation.surface: Advice to keep something drier on one side than the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one side rather than the other' swaps L (left) for R (right) in TOWEL. A keep is the strong central tower of a castle, and 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle keep is an example of a fortified tower, hence the 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Left with this, as the enemy hasn't caught up?

definitions.text: Left with this, as the enemy hasn't caught up?

parts.words: Left with this, as the enemy hasn't caught up?
parts.note: the enemy is time, and someone who has not yet been overtaken by it has spare hours with nothing to do

explanation.surface: Someone left behind because the enemy has not yet arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is proverbially 'the enemy'; if it has not caught up with you, you still hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have time on one's hands is to have spare time with nothing to fill it.

clue.text: Pale journalist grew faint

parts.note: wan means pale
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A pale reporter felt himself weakening.
explanation.definitionFit: Waned means diminished or grew weaker, like a fading moon.

clue.text: At back of boat going in circle in water sport?

indicators.note: the word for the rear of a ship is going inside the circle word

parts.note: a ring is a circle
aft means at or towards the stern of a boat

explanation.surface: Someone at the stern of a boat circling round during a water sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafting, travelling down rivers on a raft, is a water sport.

clue.text: Herb and Ian breaking record fantastically

indicators.note: Ian is breaking into the rearranged word, splitting it open
fantastically signals the letters of record being wildly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A herb and a man called Ian somehow combine to smash a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastically' turns RECORD into CORDER, and 'breaking' puts IAN into it: COR-IAN-DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is a common culinary herb, used both as leaf and seed.

clue.text: One dismissed by head cook

indicators.note: one is sent away from the word for head, leaving it shorter

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sacked by the head cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head cook' looks like one phrase, but 'head' gives CHIEF and 'cook' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook.

clue.text: Fish specially prepared, taken out of tin

indicators.note: specially suggests letters being specially reworked into a new order

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: Fish carefully prepared after being removed from a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out of tin' pretends to be canned fish but gives SN, the symbol taken from tin; it joins PREPARED in the anagram signalled by 'specially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Red snapper is a reddish sea fish popular as food.

clue.text: Being very attentive, a learner learns to subtract number?

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: a letter is subtracted from the word learns

explanation.surface: A pupil paying close attention while learning subtraction.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates are the signs British learner drivers must display.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all ears is an idiom for listening very closely.

clue.text: After a month payment limits me, so given reduction

indicators.note: the payment part comes after the month in the answer

parts.note: Dec is short for December

indicators.note: the word for payment surrounds me, limiting it

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: After a month the payments are capped, so someone gets a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrement is a decrease or reduction in amount.

clue.text: British statesman, for instance, hosted by sheep farmer?

indicators.note: the phrase for instance is held within the sheep and farmer words

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
Old MacDonald is the farmer of the nursery song
say means for instance

explanation.surface: A British politician is made welcome by a sheep farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheep farmer' reads as one person, but it splits into two pieces that hold 'for instance' between them; the farmer is Old MacDonald of the nursery song. The statesman was Britain's first Labour prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsay MacDonald was Britain's first Labour prime minister, a statesman.

clue.text: Fellow's piece of land in Midland town

parts.note: a fellow is a man, with the possessive s
a field is an enclosed piece of land

explanation.surface: A man's plot of land located in a town in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Midlands is the central region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield is a market town in Nottinghamshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: Look, with Latin one may step into someone else's job

definitions.text: one may step into someone else's job

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
cum is the Latin word for with

explanation.surface: Someone with knowledge of Latin is told to look, since they might take over another's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a stand-in, especially a doctor or cleric covering for another temporarily.

clue.text: Soldiers facing tumult, having accepted a decree

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the word for tumult takes the a into its middle

parts.note: din is a loud tumult or uproar

explanation.surface: Troops confronting an uproar after a decree has been accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is a standard crossword abbreviation for soldiers; 'facing' just places it before the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to decree or order something officially.

clue.text: Where film may be used secretly

definitions.meaning: inside a camera is where photographic film goes
a Latin legal phrase for proceedings held in private, without the public present

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally places film inside a camera, and in law means heard in private, so secretly.

clue.text: Street paintings, perhaps, feature cape in Devon

parts.note: paintings are an example of art
a point is a feature or characteristic

explanation.surface: Pavement art is a notable attraction of a Devon headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Start Point is a headland on the south coast of Devon, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Start Point is a promontory on the south Devon coast, so a cape there.

clue.text: Flighty type contriving an ego-trip

indicators.note: contriving suggests fashioning the letters of an ego-trip into something new

explanation.surface: Someone frivolous engineering a bout of self-importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty type' suggests a flighty person, but it means something that flies: a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a butterfly, a creature literally given to flight.

clue.text: Word inscribed in a ring modifying another word?

indicators.note: the word piece is written inside the others

parts.note: to dial is to ring someone up
a verb is a word

explanation.surface: A word engraved on a ring that alters the meaning of another word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverbial describes words or phrases that act as adverbs, modifying other words.

clue.text: Like old radio that comes with a hiss?

definitions.text: Like old radio that comes with a hiss?

parts.words: Like old radio that comes with a hiss?
parts.note: old-fashioned wireless was nicknamed after the vapour that powered engines, and that vapour hisses as it escapes

explanation.surface: An old radio set crackling and hissing.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam radio is a jocular British name for old-fashioned radio, and escaping steam makes a hiss.

clue.text: Performing artist once restricted by tunnel vision

indicators.note: the name is confined within the words tunnel vision, held between them

explanation.surface: A former performer whose outlook was narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was a famous singer and performer, now dead, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Chaps, I fancy, may keep quiet about female poetry

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the quiet letter within them
fancy signals the letters of chaps and I being fancifully rearranged

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: Some men think they can stay silent about women's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges CHAPS I to SAPHIC, and 'may keep' puts P (piano, quiet) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphic means relating to Sappho, the ancient Greek woman poet, or her verse.

clue.text: Mentioned two areas indoors for someone ill from damp?

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a room and an attic are two areas inside a house

explanation.surface: Someone talks about two parts of a house that make a person sick with damp.
explanation.walkthrough: ROOM + ATTIC spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheumatic is a person suffering from rheumatism, popularly blamed on damp conditions.

clue.text: Girl by no means a vehement left-winger

parts.note: mild means far from vehement
a red is a left-winger, a communist

explanation.surface: A young woman who is anything but a fiery socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a traditional English girl's name.

clue.text: Sailors very good in dance English dance they do?

indicators.note: the sailors and the very good go inside the word for a dance

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
RN is the Royal Navy
pi, short for pious, means very good

explanation.surface: Sailors are said to be very good at a particular English dance.
explanation.walkthrough: RN (Royal Navy) and PI (pious) go into HOP, then E is added. The definition leans on the clue's sailors: a hornpipe is the dance sailors are known for.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: Fate deals fool hope in half-measure

parts.note: a clot is a fool

indicators.note: only half of the word hope is taken, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Destiny gives a foolish person only half a measure of hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Clotho was one of the three Fates of Greek myth, the one who spins the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho is one of the three Fates of classical mythology, so a Fate by name.

clue.text: Significant mark made by water overflowing lake

indicators.note: the water word spills round the lake letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the tide is the rising and falling sea water

explanation.surface: A high-water mark left when a flood breaches a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A tilde is the wavy accent over n in Spanish; 'Significant' means it signifies something, not that it is important.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is a diacritic, a mark that signifies a change in sound.

clue.text: Famous person beginning to waste time

indicators.note: the time letter is wasted, thrown away from the word

parts.note: a start is a beginning

explanation.surface: A celebrity starts squandering time.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a celebrity, a famous performer.

clue.text: Beastly sound made by the people next door? Not half!

indicators.note: only half the word is wanted, so the second half is dropped

parts.note: neighbours are the people living next door

explanation.surface: Asked whether the neighbours make an animal racket, someone says emphatically that they do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it tells you to keep only half of NEIGHBOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the cry of a horse, so a sound made by a beast.

clue.text: 15 in a collection from Ancient Rome

definitions.meaning: refers to the answer to 15 down, a word acting as a modifier, which this Latin phrase is

definitions.text: in a collection from Ancient Rome
definitions.meaning: the Latin phrase means among other things, as one item within a group

explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is a Latin adverbial phrase meaning among other things, one of a collection.

clue.text: One who may have the will but won't himself succeed?

definitions.text: One who may have the will but won't himself succeed?

parts.words: One who may have the will but won't himself succeed?
parts.note: a lawyer keeps a client's testament in safe custody but does not inherit under it

explanation.surface: Someone with determination who nevertheless will not achieve success.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor often drafts and holds a client's will but is not a beneficiary.

clue.text: Frightful father about to be imprisoned

indicators.note: the word for about is locked up inside the word for father

parts.note: dad is a familiar name for a father
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A terrifying father is about to go to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be imprisoned' reads as 'soon going to jail', but 'about' is the piece and 'to be imprisoned' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread as an adjective means greatly feared, so frightful or terrible.
